jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
About Buoyant

Buoyant Aero builds and operates autonomous aerial platforms for advertising, media, and emerging dual-use applications.
We are a hardware and operations company. We design and build aircraft, move equipment and teams around the country, launch operations in new cities, work directly with customers, and operate aircraft in complex real-world environments.
We have proven that the business can work.
Our next challenge is making it scale.
We are looking for a Chief Operating Officer
who can take a fast-moving, founder-led company and build the systems, team, and operating discipline required to grow from a small number of successful operations into a national operating network.
The Role

This is not a traditional corporate COO role.
You will be responsible for turning Buoyant from a company that succeeds through individual effort and founder involvement into an organization that executes reliably through systems, processes, accountability, and strong managers.
You will own the operating machine behind the company: deployment operations, manufacturing and supply chain, logistics, people operations, financial planning, and the systems that connect them.
The right person will be equally comfortable designing an operating model for the next three years and personally fixing a broken deployment plan tomorrow morning.
What You'll OwnScale the Operating Model

Build the operating system required to grow from a handful of deployments to many simultaneous operations across the country.
Turn successful one-off processes into documented, measurable, repeatable systems.
Establish clear ownership, operating rhythms, KPIs, planning processes, and accountability across the organization.
Identify operational bottlenecks before they constrain growth.
Reduce the company's dependence on founders for day-to-day execution.

Deployment & Field Operations

Build a scalable model for launching and supporting operations in new markets.
Improve deployment planning, staffing, logistics, equipment movement, customer coordination, and operational readiness.
Develop systems that allow multiple customer operations to run simultaneously.
Drive reliability, utilization, cost efficiency, and continuous improvement across the operating network.
Work closely with flight-operations leadership while maintaining clear separation between business requirements and flight-safety authority.

Manufacturing, Supply Chain & Logistics

Build a scalable supply and production system for Buoyant's growing fleet.
Improve sourcing, supplier management, inventory planning, production scheduling, and logistics.
Develop strategies for reducing lead times, supply risk, and unnecessary complexity.
Lead efforts to onshore or dual-source critical components where it makes operational and economic sense.
Improve the flow of aircraft, parts, equipment, and consumables between manufacturing locations and operating markets.
Build the infrastructure necessary to move from prototype-style production toward repeatable fleet manufacturing.

People & Organization

Build and manage a high-performing organization as the company grows.
Develop the managers and organizational structure required to scale beyond direct founder management.
Establish clear responsibilities, expectations, and performance standards.
Build recruiting processes capable of hiring quickly without lowering the talent bar.
Make difficult personnel decisions decisively when someone is not succeeding in their role.
Create an organization where accountability is clear and problems are surfaced early.

Financial & Business Operations

Own company budgeting, operating forecasts, resource planning, and financial accountability in partnership with the founders and finance resources.
Develop clear visibility into operating costs, deployment economics, manufacturing costs, staffing requirements, and cash needs.
Translate company strategy into operating plans and budgets.
Build decision-making systems that allow the company to allocate people and capital intelligently.
Help leadership understand what the company can realistically execute and what tradeoffs are required.

Founder & Leadership Partnership

The founders are fast-moving, entrepreneurial, and highly involved in the business. The COO will complement that style by creating structure without creating bureaucracy.
You should be comfortable:
Turning ambitious ideas into executable plans.
Saying "not yet" when priorities exceed organizational capacity.
Creating clarity when plans are changing quickly.
Holding leaders accountable to commitments.
Making decisions with incomplete information.
Bringing order to situations that initially look messy.
Preserving speed while eliminating unnecessary chaos.

We want someone who makes the company faster because it is organized
, not slower because it has more process.
What We're Looking For

Required

Significant senior operating leadership experience.
Experience scaling a physical-world business from a small number of working operations into a substantially larger operating system.
Experience managing complex, distributed operations.
Experience with hardware, manufacturing, logistics, field operations, or another business where physical things must reliably move through the world.
Strong supply-chain and operational-optimization experience.
Experience building and managing growing teams.
Demonstrated ability to recruit and build teams quickly.
Demonstrated willingness to address underperformance and make difficult personnel decisions.
Strong financial and analytical instincts.
Ability to move comfortably between strategic planning and extremely hands-on problem solving.
High personal organization and exceptional follow-through.
Ability to operate effectively in an ambiguous, rapidly changing startup environment.

Particularly Valuable

Experience scaling something like:
One operating location into many.
A prototype or early-production hardware business into repeatable production.
A small field-operations team into a distributed national workforce.
Tens of employees into hundreds.
A founder-dependent company into a professionally managed organization.

We care more about having personally lived through this transition
than having worked at a large company after the hard scaling work was already complete.
Nice to Have

Aviation or airline operations experience.
Aerospace, drones, robotics, autonomous systems, or advanced hardware experience.
Experience operating regulated systems.
Experience with fleet businesses.
Experience onshoring manufacturing or restructuring a supply chain.
Experience with government or defense customers.

Aerospace experience is helpful, but it is not required. We would rather hire an exceptional operator from another complex physical-world business than a mediocre executive who happens to come from aerospace.
Who Will Thrive Here

You are probably a strong fit if:
Messy situations make you want to organize them.
You like building systems more than talking about systems.
You have unusually high standards for follow-through.
You are comfortable challenging founders.
You don't need a large staff before you can make progress.
You can negotiate a supplier contract in the morning, interview an operations leader in the afternoon, and review next year's operating plan that evening.
You know when a process is necessary and when a process should simply be deleted.
You believe speed and discipline reinforce each other rather than compete.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months:
Buoyant can execute multiple simultaneous operations without constant founder coordination.

Manufacturing, supply chain, staffing, deployment logistics, and financial planning operate from clear systems and forecasts rather than emergencies.

The organization has strong functional owners, clear accountability, and the management infrastructure required for the next stage of growth.

The ultimate measure of success is simple:
Buoyant should be able to grow dramatically without becoming dramatically more chaotic.

Compensation

Competitive executive salary plus meaningful equity, commensurate with experience.
This is an opportunity to build the operating foundation of an unusual company at the point where the challenge is shifting from proving that something can work to proving that it can work at scale.

jobs.title: Associate Executive Director, NYC
jobs.description:
If working for an organization that supports the land and people of Israel excites you, then join us and you needn't wait another minute to change the world!

Position Overview:

Jewish National Fund-USA is expanding its Tristate fundraising team and adding several new positions to support our growing donor community and organizational impact.

We are seeking an experienced Associate Executive Director to oversee fundraising and community engagement in Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens.
This role focuses on building and sustaining strong donor relationships, partnering closely with lay leadership, and expanding regional support through strategic cultivation, events, and mission-based engagement.

Reports to: Executive Director, Tristate
Location: New York, NY (on-site, 5 days)

Responsibilities:

Regional Leadership & Strategy
Develop and execute a regional fundraising and engagement strategy aligned with national priorities
Set and manage revenue goals, performance metrics, and accountability standards
Serve as a senior representative of JNF-USA within the regional Jewish community

Fundraising & Donor Engagement
Manage and grow a portfolio of major donors and prospects through strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship
Identify and develop new donor relationships to expand the regional pipeline
Partner with lay leadership and board members to leverage networks and advance fundraising outcomes
Oversee cultivation initiatives, donor briefings, events, missions, and stewardship activities

Team Leadership & Collaboration
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing regional team
Support hiring, onboarding, coaching, and performance management
Collaborate with national development, marketing, finance, and program teams

Community Engagement & Representation
Build and maintain strong relationships with communal partners and stakeholders
Recruit and engage participants for missions, conferences, and signature initiatives
Host visiting Israeli partners and affiliates with appropriate donor alignment and follow-up

Operations, Data & Reporting
Ensure accurate donor activity tracking and reporting in Salesforce
Use data and analytics to support forecasting, strategy, and performance management
Oversee regional budgets and responsible resource management

Qualifications:

Deep passion for Israel and JNF-USA's mission
10+ years of progressive fundraising, development, or related leadership experience, including major gifts
Proven ability to develop strategy and drive revenue growth
Strong executive-level written and verbal communication skills
Demonstrated experience managing and developing teams
Strategic, organized, and comfortable operating with autonomy
Salesforce or CRM preferred
Familiarity with the regional Jewish community and nonprofit landscape strongly preferred

Travel:

Regular regional travel within the assigned territory
Occasional domestic and international travel, including missions to Israel and national conferences

Perks:

Days off for all work-prohibitive Jewish holidays, in addition to the secular US holidays
Generous paid time off
3pm close-of-business on Fridays
Top-notch healthcare (including dental and vision)
Parental Leave policy
Employer-paid life insurance
Employer-paid short and long-term disability
403(b) with 10.5% employer contribution
Opportunities to travel to Israel
Occasional domestic and international travel, including missions to Israel and national conferences

Compensation:

$175,000–$210,000

Pay Type:

Salaried

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role.

WHAT WE DO

For 125 years, Jewish National Fund-USA has helped strengthen the land and people of Israel by investing in the communities, infrastructure, and leadership that shape the country's future. Our work is focused on making Israel's North and South places where families can build full, vibrant lives with access to medical care, emergency response, water solutions, parks, playgrounds, jobs, and economic opportunity. Working with our donors and partners, we support underpopulated communities, help attract new residents, improve quality of life, and create the conditions for long-term growth. Our work reaches beyond projects on the ground. Through education, travel, and leadership opportunities, we connect Americans of all ages to Israel in meaningful and lasting ways. That vision continues with the World Zionist Village in Be'er Sheva, a global center that will bring people together to live, learn, lead, and strengthen the next generation of Zionist leadership. From urgent relief to long-term transformation, Jewish National Fund-USA is helping build a stronger future for Israel and creating lasting legacies for generations to come. Learn more at jnf.org.

SINCE 1901, JNF HAS:

• Planted more than 250 million trees
• Built over 250 reservoirs and dams
• Developed over 250,000 acres of land
• Created more than 2,000 parks
• Provided the infrastructure for over 1,000 communities
• Connected thousands of children and young adults to Israel and their heritage
Jewish National Fund prides itself on honoring the pioneers of the past and celebrating their spirit by continuing the pioneering tradition in the areas of technology, environmental progress, community development, water renewal and building the land of Israel for many years to come.
Jewish National Fund affirms the bonds of the Jewish family with their strength of unity, the understanding that each member can make a difference and the collective power to build prosperity, develop innovative solutions and promote the greater good.

OUR CREDENTIALS & PARTNERSHIPS

A registered 501(c)(3) organization, Jewish National Fund is recognized as a 4-star organization by Charity Navigator, America's leading independent charity evaluator, for its sound fiscal management, accountability, and transparency. JNF has also been rated a top charity by the American Institute of Philanthropy and meets the 20 rigorous standards of the Better Business Bureau (BBB) Wise Giving Alliance, and the transparency standards of Tzedakah, Inc. No other Jewish organization meets all these standards.

OUR CULTURE

We are Vi Zion
-driven relationship-based, fast-paced, and Positively Israel!
OUR CORE VALUES

Be Bold:
Beyond. We are proud and passionate, vocal, and visionary about Israel and Zionism. We pride ourselves on our out-of-the-box thinking and the great things it accomplishes for the land and with the people of Israel.

Belong:
Stay long. We are an inclusive and diverse workplace welcoming and respecting all cultures, ages, religions, ethnicities, genders, orientations, and physical abilities. Understanding that a work-life balance is crucial to the success of our organization, we are empathetic, understanding, caring, appreciative, and respectful of one another as we strive to develop and retain our professionals and donors for the long-run.
Be Inscribed:
Be the Impact. To walk in the land of Israel and see the impact of our work instills the greatest sense of fulfillment. We strive for each employee to make their mark, leave their footprint, be heard, and feel relevant as together we help ensure the vibrancy of Israel for the next 100 years. We plant the future, not just trees.

Be Kind:
Act with Chesed. At JNF-USA we do not underestimate the power of kindness. We use recognition and praise to motivate teams, individuals, donors, and stakeholders. We are proud of our please and thank you's. We listen and lend a helping hand when a co-worker is challenged. Whether random or deliberate acts, kindness is a key ingredient to our positive workplace and mindset.
B'Yachad:
Together. Great collaboration between our employees, donors and affiliates in Israel is a priority: everyone matters no matter their role. We recognize that open and inspirational communication, teamwork, and collegiality is a force multiplier in reaching our goals, mission, and vision. Jewish National Fund-USA exemplifies the power of unity.

jobs.title: President and CEO
jobs.description:
Jorgenson Pace has been retained to conduct this search.

The Position

The President reports directly to the Board of Directors of Mohawk Valley EDGE and works closely with affiliated economic development partners and regional stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Organizational Management

·        Lead the development and execution of Mohawk Valley EDGE’s long-range economic development strategy, including business attraction, retention, and expansion, site readiness, redevelopment, and sector-based growth initiatives.
·        Preserve the organization’s core strengths in project execution, public-private collaboration, and results-oriented economic development while advancing a clear, compelling vision for the future.
·        Provide executive leadership to staff; set clear priorities; define roles; delegate meaningfully; and ensure consistent coordination across economic development, project development, planning, marketing, and finance functions.
·        Build and sustain a high-trust internal culture that values staff engagement, professional development, burnout prevention, and talent retention as strategic priorities.
·        Oversee an organization whose financial model includes both grant-supported and program-service-supported activity, ensuring strong stewardship of externally funded initiatives, earned-service work, and major development-related commitments.
·        Partner with the Board of Directors on strategic planning, annual priorities, budgeting, governance, and performance reporting, delivering clear, organized, and consistent communication.
·        Oversee management services contracts for Griffiss Local Development Corporation, Oneida County Industrial Development Corporation, and Rome Industrial Development Corporation.

Business Attraction, Expansion & Regional Positioning

·        Lead coordinated business attraction and expansion efforts, including direct engagement with corporate executives, consultants, developers, and national site selectors regarding investment, expansion, relocation, and redevelopment opportunities.
·        Serve as the region’s chief storyteller, crafting and delivering a compelling narrative that positions the Mohawk Valley as a destination of choice for business investment, grounded in location, infrastructure, workforce, industry assets, and development readiness.
·        Represent Mohawk Valley EDGE at trade shows, business development events, and strategic outreach opportunities to generate project leads and strengthen market visibility.
·        Oversee and strengthen outreach-driven business development activity, including company engagement and prospect cultivation.

Project Development, Real Estate & Infrastructure

·        Provide leadership and oversight for the organization’s active site and redevelopment portfolio, including projects such as the St. Luke’s Redevelopment at the former MVHS Hospital Campus in New Hartford, Marcy Nanocenter, multiple available sites, and brownfield cleanup and revitalization efforts.
·        Guide real estate development and transaction activity involving leases, sales, development agreements, and project terms associated with business growth and redevelopment.
·        Coordinate capital improvement and infrastructure efforts needed to improve site competitiveness and project readiness.

Finance, Incentives & Deal Structuring

·        Structure and negotiate public-private financing packages, incentive strategies, and transaction frameworks that support business attraction, retention, redevelopment, and strategic investment projects, drawing on a sophisticated understanding of the full range of public and private financial pathways available to attract capital to the region.
·        Review and analyze financial statements, underwriting materials, project budgets, and economic impact considerations relevant to major projects and business opportunities.
·        Assist in the development of grants, funding applications, and financing strategies involving local, state, federal, and private sources.
·        Ensure organizational decisions and development activities are grounded in sound financial analysis, disciplined project evaluation, and measurable results.

Regional & Statewide Coordination

·        Maintain strong working knowledge of the Mohawk Valley Regional Economic Development Council structure, priorities, and related New York State economic development processes, and use that knowledge to strengthen project competitiveness.
·        Work effectively across the full six-county Mohawk Valley region and build productive relationships with county leaders, municipal officials, industrial development agencies, employers, developers, educational institutions, and other regional stakeholders.
·        Build and maintain trusted relationships with local, state, and federal agencies and partner organizations to advance major projects and secure supportive resources for development.

Industry Strategy & Regional Strengths

·        Advance business attraction, retention, and project development strategies that reflect the Mohawk Valley’s established and emerging strengths in advanced manufacturing, agribusiness and food-related production, materials and metals manufacturing, and cyber/information technology.
·        Communicate the value of the region’s assets—including strategic location, major development sites, academic and research institutions, transportation access, cybersecurity presence, semiconductor-related investments, agribusiness opportunity, and manufacturing capability—to corporate prospects, site selectors, investment partners, and public agencies.
·        Collaborate with workforce, education, and training partners to support employer needs and align talent resources with opportunities in the region’s priority sectors.

Knowledge, Skills, and Traits                                  

Leadership Traits

·         Strategic Vision & Direction Setter:

The Rockefeller Foundation Communications team advances the Foundation's mission by strengthening understanding of its priorities, amplifying impact, and engaging key audiences through strategic communications, digital engagement, content development, and stakeholder outreach.

What We Seek:

Join a dynamic team of development professionals working to advance the mission of the University of New Mexico. The UNM Foundation seeks nominations and applications for the position of Director of Development for the UNM College of Nursing.
As the leader of Nursing Education in the State of New Mexico, UNM’s College of Nursing offers an unmatched depth and breadth of education, research, service, and leadership within the field of Nursing.
The successful applicant will be responsible for creating and implementing a comprehensive development program in coordination with the leadership of the UNM College of Nursing, the UNM Foundation staff, and colleagues. About the University

Founded in 1889 as New Mexico’s flagship institution, the University of New Mexico (www.unm.edu) has nearly 170,000 alumni from its culturally rich 12 Colleges and Schools, which offer over 215 degree and certificate programs. UNM is the only Hispanic-Serving Institution in the U.S. that is also classified a Carnegie Research University with Very High Activity. Recently, Hispanic Business Magazine ranked four University schools among the top 10 including the UNM School of Law, Anderson School of Management, the UNM School of Medicine and the UNM School of Engineering.
The University now occupies nearly 800 acres near old Route 66 in the heart of Albuquerque, a dynamic multi-cultural Southwestern city. Albuquerque and its surrounding area is the largest metropolitan region in New Mexico, known for high-tech industry, the world renowned international Balloon Fiesta, and its devotion to the UNM campus, programs, and athletics.

About the College of Nursing

In the early 1950s, New Mexico nurses voiced their concerns about an inadequate supply of registered nurses (RNs) to meet the health care needs of the state’s growing population. By the spring of 1955, the UNM College of Nursing was founded by Dr. Marion Fleck and Mary Jane Carter, with the enthusiastic support of UNM President Tom Popejoy.
Today, the UNM College of Nursing has over 1300 students in BSN, DNP, and PhD programs. We are the #1 BSN Program in New Mexico and rank in the top 17% in the nation. Our DNP Nurse-Midwifery program ranks #7 in the Nation. We give over $1.2M in scholarships each year and 83% of our students receive some form of financial aid. 71% of our students identify and coming from underrepresented groups.

The Rockefeller Foundation Communications team advances the Foundation's mission by strengthening understanding of its priorities, amplifying impact, and engaging key audiences through strategic communications, digital engagement, content development, and stakeholder outreach.

The Managing Director, Media Relations leads how The Rockefeller Foundation earns visibility and safeguards its reputation in a rapidly evolving media and information environment. The role sets the Foundation's media relations and press strategy, shapes its approach to executive visibility and reputational risk, and ensures a clear, credible, and consistent institutional voice across audiences and platforms. Reporting to the SVP, Communications, the Managing Director serves as a senior advisor to Foundation leadership and leads enterprise-wide media initiatives, working across the Foundation to strengthen its engagement with journalists and other key stakeholders in support of its mission and strategic priorities.

Work Schedule
: This role is on a hybrid work schedule and is required to be in the office on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. The role can be based in either the Washington, DC, or New York City office, with a preference for the New York City office.

Pay Range:
$230,000 - $280,000. This represents the present low and high end of the Foundation’s pay range for this position. Actual pay will vary based on various factors, including but not limited to experience.

Develop and lead the Foundation's media relations strategy—setting priorities, frameworks, and standards for media engagement, and translating institutional priorities into integrated media approaches—to strengthen visibility, reputation, and stakeholder engagement in support of mission impact across evolving news, digital, and emerging media channels.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Foundation’s President and senior executives on media engagement, messaging, and public visibility—including media pitching, message development, and preparation for interviews and high-profile media events.
Shape and safeguard the Foundation's institutional narrative, ensuring talking points and messages stay consistent and in sync across Programs, Teams, and Regional Offices.
Position Foundation leaders and experts as authoritative voices with the media—providing coaching and strategic counsel and building and managing the public profiles of the President and senior leaders through high-impact op-eds, bylined pieces, speaking platforms, and executive profiles that advance institutional priorities.
Approve Foundation press releases, media statements, and briefing materials, and serve as a Foundation spokesperson when needed.
Oversee the day-to-day operations of the press office, ensuring rapid, accurate, and coordinated responses to inbound media inquiries.
Anticipate and manage reputational risk, detecting emerging issues early and leading crisis communications with clarity and speed, including partnering with the General Counsel on adversarial press, litigation-related communications, and sensitive disclosures.
Cultivate and manage relationships with journalists and media outlets, using coverage insights, analytics, and emerging trends to inform the most strategic pitching and outlet choices.
Provide strategic oversight of media relations operations, including budget management and agency/vendor relationships for wire services, media monitoring, and select media sponsorship opportunities.
Establish effective systems, governance structures, and operating practices that improve the efficiency, accountability, and quality of the Foundation's media function.
Partner with senior leaders across the Foundation and coordinate closely with program focal points and Regional Office colleagues to advance major media moments and high-profile events.
Manage outside consultants and agencies engaged for media pitching and strategic advice, and coordinate closely with internal teammates—including Digital and Internal Communications—to ensure an integrated, consistent approach across channels.
Provide strategic leadership and oversight to the Media Relations team and external consultants—building leadership capability, fostering collaboration, and coaching team members to create an inclusive, high-performing culture aligned with Foundation priorities, values, and performance expectations.

Generally expected to have 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in media relations, journalism, public affairs, or related fields, including significant leadership experience—ideally representing an organization with the media, serving as a spokesperson, or working for a top-tier news organization.

Experience working within philanthropy, public sector, nonprofit, international development, or similar mission-driven organizations.
Knowledge of and interest in foreign policy or international affairs.
Demonstrated success developing and leading enterprise-level media and reputation strategies for complex, mission-driven organizations.
Proven track record positioning organizations and their senior leadership, managing reputational risk, and leading crisis communications.
Experience advising senior executives and developing media approaches that influence internal and external stakeholders.
Extensive knowledge of media trends and established relationships with top-tier journalists and media outlets.
Proven ability to lead large-scale, cross-functional initiatives and drive organizational outcomes through influence and collaboration.
Strong people leadership experience, including developing talent and managing high-performing teams.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills, including public speaking and the ability to represent the Foundation with external partners.

Competencies

Action Oriented: Takes on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm.
Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Our client, a national leader in emergency medical and healthcare products, is seeking a Chief Operating Officer to own the company’s end-to-end operating model and product engine: from product concept and engineering through sourcing, manufacturing, distribution, and customer support. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving on the Senior Leadership Team, the COO is the executive who turns enterprise strategy into measurable operational results — sustainable growth, margin expansion, regulatory compliance, and an exceptional customer experience for the first responders and healthcare professionals our client serves nationwide.
This is a build-and-scale mandate, not a caretaker role. The right leader will strengthen and expand our client’s manufacturing, distribution, and operational infrastructure; bring new technology and automation into the business; integrate acquisitions; and develop the next generation of operating leaders — all while holding the line on quality, safety, and compliance in a regulated medical environment.
What You Will Own

Enterprise Operations

Lead all core operating functions — Purchasing, Supply Chain, Customer Care, Warehousing, Distribution, Logistics, Engineering, Manufacturing, Assembly/Kitting, and Contract Manufacturing Management — with full accountability for performance, quality, cost, service levels, compliance, and scalability.
Define and execute the company’s operational, engineering, and manufacturing strategies in alignment with corporate objectives, growth plans, and shareholder expectations.
Design, optimize, and expand our client’s distribution, manufacturing, and operational footprint to support current and future business requirements.
Establish and monitor the KPI framework for customer satisfaction, quality, productivity, on-time delivery, inventory, safety, service levels, and profitability; report performance and risk regularly to the CEO and Board of Directors.
Serve as the executive escalation point for critical operational, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and customer experience issues.

Product, Engineering, and Manufacturing

Provide executive leadership over the full product lifecycle — product development, design engineering, lifecycle management, and manufacturing readiness.
Ensure engineering maintains rigorous, audit-ready product development practices: design controls, risk management, technical documentation, verification and validation, and design transfer, consistent with applicable medical device regulatory and quality standards.
Oversee manufacturing operations end to end, including production planning, assembly and kitting, process optimization, automation, capacity planning, and continuous improvement.
Bring new technologies into the business to drive innovation, strengthen competitive differentiation, and increase customer value.

Partners and Supply Base

Build and govern high-performing relationships with suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers, and other strategic partners to ensure quality, reliability, scalability, and cost effectiveness.
Provide executive oversight of third-party manufacturers, including partner selection, performance management, quality oversight, contractual compliance, and ongoing operational governance.

Growth, M&A, and Leadership

Partner with the CEO and Senior Leadership Team to set enterprise priorities, evaluate business performance, and execute key strategic initiatives.
Lead operational due diligence, integration planning, organizational alignment, and value realization for mergers, acquisitions, and other strategic growth initiatives.
Drive operational excellence through performance measurement, standardization, technology enablement, and Lean business practices.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing operations leadership team; own succession planning and leadership development across the operating organization.
Champion a culture of safety, quality, accountability, innovation, and customer focus, and advance our client’s Mission, Vision, Values, and Guiding Principles.
Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Finance, IT, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Human Resources, Legal, and Compliance to ensure enterprise-wide alignment.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12–24 months, the COO will be measured on outcomes such as:A unified, scalable operating model across purchasing, supply chain, distribution, and manufacturing with clear ownership and a single set of performance metrics.
Measurable improvement in margin, productivity, on-time delivery, inventory performance, and customer satisfaction.
Product development and manufacturing processes that are consistently audit-ready and compliant with applicable medical device requirements.
Successful operational integration of acquisitions with realized synergies.
A deep, credible leadership bench with succession plans in place for every key operating role.

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following to be considered:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in medical device or healthcare products, including executive-level (VP or above) accountability for operations, manufacturing, supply chain, and customer-facing functions.
Proven success leading complex, multi-site operations in a regulated medical device, healthcare, or life sciences environment.
Direct experience leading product development organizations and bringing regulated products from concept through commercialization and lifecycle management.
Working command of medical device development and quality requirements: design controls, risk management, quality systems, and regulatory expectations.
Significant hands-on experience running manufacturing, assembly, and kitting operations, including production planning, operational scaling, and contract manufacturing relationships.
Demonstrated results driving operational excellence, continuous improvement, productivity gains, margin expansion, and organizational scalability using Lean, Six Sigma, or comparable methodologies.
Strong financial acumen with ownership of budgets, capital investments, operational metrics, and profitability targets.
Track record of leading large-scale organizational change and executing strategic initiatives, including M&A due diligence and integration.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA, Master’s degree in Engineering, or other relevant advanced degree.
Experience in a distribution-led business serving EMS, first responder, or acute-care customers.
Experience scaling operations in a private-equity-backed or high-growth environment.
Experience leading automation, technology enablement, or digital transformation initiatives across warehouse, manufacturing, or supply chain operations.

Leadership Profile

Executive presence and Board-level communication skills; able to represent the company credibly with customers, suppliers, partners, investors, and regulators.
Builder of high-performing teams and developer of leaders, with a bias for accountability and clear ownership.
Analytical, decisive, and strategic, with the operational discipline to balance innovation, quality, compliance, customer satisfaction, and financial performance simultaneously.
Entrepreneurial and hands-on: comfortable on the warehouse and production floor as well as in the boardroom.
Unquestioned integrity and ethical leadership.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

This is an on-site executive role based in Dublin, Ohio, with regular presence in warehouse, manufacturing, and distribution facilities. The role requires approximately 30% travel (primarily domestic, occasional international); the ability to move throughout office and operational environments for extended periods and comply with all facility safety requirements; standard use of a computer and communication tools; occasional lifting of up to 20 pounds; and the ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive business information. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Benefits Snapshot

This role offers the chance to join a team that genuinely enjoys the work they do, contributing to a mission that helps protect and save lives. The company is steady, essential, and continuing to grow, with a strong commitment to diversity, inclusion, and sustainability. Its culture is built around its people and the things they care about, featuring perks like bring-your-dog-to-work days, travel discounts, gym membership discounts, and happy hours. The benefits package is comprehensive, including flexible PTO, a full range of health and wellness coverage, 401(k) matching, tuition assistance, adoption support, and pet insurance.
About Our Client

Our client’s mission is to be the best partner for those who save and improve patients’ lives. The company serves first responders and healthcare professionals nationwide, and excellence in delivering on that mission depends on a diverse, empowered team that brings its full, authentic self to work each day.
Our client is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We offer a competitive salary, commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package, including a 401(k) Plan. new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
About Buoyant

Buoyant Aero builds and operates autonomous aerial platforms for advertising, media, and emerging dual-use applications.
We are a hardware and operations company. We design and build aircraft, move equipment and teams around the country, launch operations in new cities, work directly with customers, and operate aircraft in complex real-world environments.
We have proven that the business can work.
Our next challenge is making it scale.
We are looking for a Chief Operating Officer
who can take a fast-moving, founder-led company and build the systems, team, and operating discipline required to grow from a small number of successful operations into a national operating network.
The Role

This is not a traditional corporate COO role.
You will be responsible for turning Buoyant from a company that succeeds through individual effort and founder involvement into an organization that executes reliably through systems, processes, accountability, and strong managers.
You will own the operating machine behind the company: deployment operations, manufacturing and supply chain, logistics, people operations, financial planning, and the systems that connect them.
The right person will be equally comfortable designing an operating model for the next three years and personally fixing a broken deployment plan tomorrow morning.
What You'll OwnScale the Operating Model

Build the operating system required to grow from a handful of deployments to many simultaneous operations across the country.
Turn successful one-off processes into documented, measurable, repeatable systems.
Establish clear ownership, operating rhythms, KPIs, planning processes, and accountability across the organization.
Identify operational bottlenecks before they constrain growth.
Reduce the company's dependence on founders for day-to-day execution.

Deployment & Field Operations

Build a scalable model for launching and supporting operations in new markets.
Improve deployment planning, staffing, logistics, equipment movement, customer coordination, and operational readiness.
Develop systems that allow multiple customer operations to run simultaneously.
Drive reliability, utilization, cost efficiency, and continuous improvement across the operating network.
Work closely with flight-operations leadership while maintaining clear separation between business requirements and flight-safety authority.

Manufacturing, Supply Chain & Logistics

Build a scalable supply and production system for Buoyant's growing fleet.
Improve sourcing, supplier management, inventory planning, production scheduling, and logistics.
Develop strategies for reducing lead times, supply risk, and unnecessary complexity.
Lead efforts to onshore or dual-source critical components where it makes operational and economic sense.
Improve the flow of aircraft, parts, equipment, and consumables between manufacturing locations and operating markets.
Build the infrastructure necessary to move from prototype-style production toward repeatable fleet manufacturing.

People & Organization

Build and manage a high-performing organization as the company grows.
Develop the managers and organizational structure required to scale beyond direct founder management.
Establish clear responsibilities, expectations, and performance standards.
Build recruiting processes capable of hiring quickly without lowering the talent bar.
Make difficult personnel decisions decisively when someone is not succeeding in their role.
Create an organization where accountability is clear and problems are surfaced early.

Financial & Business Operations

Own company budgeting, operating forecasts, resource planning, and financial accountability in partnership with the founders and finance resources.
Develop clear visibility into operating costs, deployment economics, manufacturing costs, staffing requirements, and cash needs.
Translate company strategy into operating plans and budgets.
Build decision-making systems that allow the company to allocate people and capital intelligently.
Help leadership understand what the company can realistically execute and what tradeoffs are required.

Founder & Leadership Partnership

The founders are fast-moving, entrepreneurial, and highly involved in the business. The COO will complement that style by creating structure without creating bureaucracy.
You should be comfortable:
Turning ambitious ideas into executable plans.
Saying "not yet" when priorities exceed organizational capacity.
Creating clarity when plans are changing quickly.
Holding leaders accountable to commitments.
Making decisions with incomplete information.
Bringing order to situations that initially look messy.
Preserving speed while eliminating unnecessary chaos.

We want someone who makes the company faster because it is organized
, not slower because it has more process.
What We're Looking For

Required

Significant senior operating leadership experience.
Experience scaling a physical-world business from a small number of working operations into a substantially larger operating system.
Experience managing complex, distributed operations.
Experience with hardware, manufacturing, logistics, field operations, or another business where physical things must reliably move through the world.
Strong supply-chain and operational-optimization experience.
Experience building and managing growing teams.
Demonstrated ability to recruit and build teams quickly.
Demonstrated willingness to address underperformance and make difficult personnel decisions.
Strong financial and analytical instincts.
Ability to move comfortably between strategic planning and extremely hands-on problem solving.
High personal organization and exceptional follow-through.
Ability to operate effectively in an ambiguous, rapidly changing startup environment.

Particularly Valuable

Experience scaling something like:
One operating location into many.
A prototype or early-production hardware business into repeatable production.
A small field-operations team into a distributed national workforce.
Tens of employees into hundreds.
A founder-dependent company into a professionally managed organization.

We care more about having personally lived through this transition
than having worked at a large company after the hard scaling work was already complete.
Nice to Have

Aviation or airline operations experience.
Aerospace, drones, robotics, autonomous systems, or advanced hardware experience.
Experience operating regulated systems.
Experience with fleet businesses.
Experience onshoring manufacturing or restructuring a supply chain.
Experience with government or defense customers.

Aerospace experience is helpful, but it is not required. We would rather hire an exceptional operator from another complex physical-world business than a mediocre executive who happens to come from aerospace.
Who Will Thrive Here

You are probably a strong fit if:
Messy situations make you want to organize them.
You like building systems more than talking about systems.
You have unusually high standards for follow-through.
You are comfortable challenging founders.
You don't need a large staff before you can make progress.
You can negotiate a supplier contract in the morning, interview an operations leader in the afternoon, and review next year's operating plan that evening.
You know when a process is necessary and when a process should simply be deleted.
You believe speed and discipline reinforce each other rather than compete.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months:
Buoyant can execute multiple simultaneous operations without constant founder coordination.

Manufacturing, supply chain, staffing, deployment logistics, and financial planning operate from clear systems and forecasts rather than emergencies.

The organization has strong functional owners, clear accountability, and the management infrastructure required for the next stage of growth.

The ultimate measure of success is simple:
Buoyant should be able to grow dramatically without becoming dramatically more chaotic.

Compensation

Competitive executive salary plus meaningful equity, commensurate with experience.
This is an opportunity to build the operating foundation of an unusual company at the point where the challenge is shifting from proving that something can work to proving that it can work at scale.

We are seeking an experienced Associate Executive Director to oversee fundraising and community engagement in Manhattan, the Bronx, Brooklyn, Queens.
This role focuses on building and sustaining strong donor relationships, partnering closely with lay leadership, and expanding regional support through strategic cultivation, events, and mission-based engagement.

Reports to: Executive Director, Tristate
Location: New York, NY (on-site, 5 days)

Regional Leadership & Strategy
Develop and execute a regional fundraising and engagement strategy aligned with national priorities
Set and manage revenue goals, performance metrics, and accountability standards
Serve as a senior representative of JNF-USA within the regional Jewish community

Fundraising & Donor Engagement
Manage and grow a portfolio of major donors and prospects through strategic cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship
Identify and develop new donor relationships to expand the regional pipeline
Partner with lay leadership and board members to leverage networks and advance fundraising outcomes
Oversee cultivation initiatives, donor briefings, events, missions, and stewardship activities

Team Leadership & Collaboration
Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing regional team
Support hiring, onboarding, coaching, and performance management
Collaborate with national development, marketing, finance, and program teams

Community Engagement & Representation
Build and maintain strong relationships with communal partners and stakeholders
Recruit and engage participants for missions, conferences, and signature initiatives
Host visiting Israeli partners and affiliates with appropriate donor alignment and follow-up

Operations, Data & Reporting
Ensure accurate donor activity tracking and reporting in Salesforce
Use data and analytics to support forecasting, strategy, and performance management
Oversee regional budgets and responsible resource management

Qualifications:

Deep passion for Israel and JNF-USA's mission
10+ years of progressive fundraising, development, or related leadership experience, including major gifts
Proven ability to develop strategy and drive revenue growth
Strong executive-level written and verbal communication skills
Demonstrated experience managing and developing teams
Strategic, organized, and comfortable operating with autonomy
Salesforce or CRM preferred
Familiarity with the regional Jewish community and nonprofit landscape strongly preferred

Regular regional travel within the assigned territory
Occasional domestic and international travel, including missions to Israel and national conferences

Days off for all work-prohibitive Jewish holidays, in addition to the secular US holidays
Generous paid time off
3pm close-of-business on Fridays
Top-notch healthcare (including dental and vision)
Parental Leave policy
Employer-paid life insurance
Employer-paid short and long-term disability
403(b) with 10.5% employer contribution
Opportunities to travel to Israel

Salaried

Salaries will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and qualifications for the role.

WHAT WE DO

For 125 years, Jewish National Fund-USA has helped strengthen the land and people of Israel by investing in the communities, infrastructure, and leadership that shape the country's future. Our work is focused on making Israel's North and South places where families can build full, vibrant lives with access to medical care, emergency response, water solutions, parks, playgrounds, jobs, and economic opportunity. Working with our donors and partners, we support underpopulated communities, help attract new residents, improve quality of life, and create the conditions for long-term growth. Our work reaches beyond projects on the ground. Through education, travel, and leadership opportunities, we connect Americans of all ages to Israel in meaningful and lasting ways. From urgent relief to long-term transformation, Jewish National Fund-USA is helping build a stronger future for Israel and creating lasting legacies for generations to come. Learn more at jnf.org.

• Planted more than 250 million trees
• Built over 250 reservoirs and dams
• Developed over 250,000 acres of land
• Created more than 2,000 parks
• Provided the infrastructure for over 1,000 communities
• Connected thousands of children and young adults to Israel and their heritage

Jewish National Fund affirms the bonds of the Jewish family with their strength of unity, the understanding that each member can make a difference and the collective power to build prosperity, develop innovative solutions and promote the greater good.

-driven relationship-based, fast-paced, and Positively Israel!

Beyond. We are proud and passionate, vocal, and visionary about Israel and Zionism. We pride ourselves on our out-of-the-box thinking and the great things it accomplishes for the land and with the people of Israel.

Be the Impact. To walk in the land of Israel and see the impact of our work instills the greatest sense of fulfillment. We strive for each employee to make their mark, leave their footprint, be heard, and feel relevant as together we help ensure the vibrancy of Israel for the next 100 years. We plant the future, not just trees.

We are proud of our please and thank you's. We listen and lend a helping hand when a co-worker is challenged. Whether random or deliberate acts, kindness is a key ingredient to our positive workplace and mindset.

·        Lead the development and execution of Mohawk Valley EDGE’s long-range economic development strategy, including business attraction, retention, and expansion, site readiness, redevelopment, and sector-based growth initiatives.
·        Preserve the organization’s core strengths in project execution, public-private collaboration, and results-oriented economic development while advancing a clear, compelling vision for the future.
·        Provide executive leadership to staff; set clear priorities; define roles; delegate meaningfully; and ensure consistent coordination across economic development, project development, planning, marketing, and finance functions.
·        Build and sustain a high-trust internal culture that values staff engagement, professional development, burnout prevention, and talent retention as strategic priorities.
·        Oversee an organization whose financial model includes both grant-supported and program-service-supported activity, ensuring strong stewardship of externally funded initiatives, earned-service work, and major development-related commitments.
·        Partner with the Board of Directors on strategic planning, annual priorities, budgeting, governance, and performance reporting, delivering clear, organized, and consistent communication.
·        Oversee management services contracts for Griffiss Local Development Corporation, Oneida County Industrial Development Corporation, and Rome Industrial Development Corporation.

·        Lead coordinated business attraction and expansion efforts, including direct engagement with corporate executives, consultants, developers, and national site selectors regarding investment, expansion, relocation, and redevelopment opportunities.
·        Serve as the region’s chief storyteller, crafting and delivering a compelling narrative that positions the Mohawk Valley as a destination of choice for business investment, grounded in location, infrastructure, workforce, industry assets, and development readiness.
·        Represent Mohawk Valley EDGE at trade shows, business development events, and strategic outreach opportunities to generate project leads and strengthen market visibility.
·        Oversee and strengthen outreach-driven business development activity, including company engagement and prospect cultivation.

Project Development, Real Estate & Infrastructure

·        Provide leadership and oversight for the organization’s active site and redevelopment portfolio, including projects such as the St. Luke’s Redevelopment at the former MVHS Hospital Campus in New Hartford, Marcy Nanocenter, multiple available sites, and brownfield cleanup and revitalization efforts.
·        Guide real estate development and transaction activity involving leases, sales, development agreements, and project terms associated with business growth and redevelopment.
·        Coordinate capital improvement and infrastructure efforts needed to improve site competitiveness and project readiness.

Finance, Incentives & Deal Structuring

·        Structure and negotiate public-private financing packages, incentive strategies, and transaction frameworks that support business attraction, retention, redevelopment, and strategic investment projects, drawing on a sophisticated understanding of the full range of public and private financial pathways available to attract capital to the region.
·        Review and analyze financial statements, underwriting materials, project budgets, and economic impact considerations relevant to major projects and business opportunities.
·        Assist in the development of grants, funding applications, and financing strategies involving local, state, federal, and private sources.
·        Ensure organizational decisions and development activities are grounded in sound financial analysis, disciplined project evaluation, and measurable results.

Regional & Statewide Coordination

·        Maintain strong working knowledge of the Mohawk Valley Regional Economic Development Council structure, priorities, and related New York State economic development processes, and use that knowledge to strengthen project competitiveness.
·        Work effectively across the full six-county Mohawk Valley region and build productive relationships with county leaders, municipal officials, industrial development agencies, employers, developers, educational institutions, and other regional stakeholders.
·        Build and maintain trusted relationships with local, state, and federal agencies and partner organizations to advance major projects and secure supportive resources for development.

Industry Strategy & Regional Strengths

·        Advance business attraction, retention, and project development strategies that reflect the Mohawk Valley’s established and emerging strengths in advanced manufacturing, agribusiness and food-related production, materials and metals manufacturing, and cyber/information technology.
·        Communicate the value of the region’s assets—including strategic location, major development sites, academic and research institutions, transportation access, cybersecurity presence, semiconductor-related investments, agribusiness opportunity, and manufacturing capability—to corporate prospects, site selectors, investment partners, and public agencies.
·        Collaborate with workforce, education, and training partners to support employer needs and align talent resources with opportunities in the region’s priority sectors.

Knowledge, Skills, and Traits                                  

Leadership Traits

·         Strategic Vision & Direction Setter:

What We Seek:

Join a dynamic team of development professionals working to advance the mission of the University of New Mexico. The UNM Foundation seeks nominations and applications for the position of Director of Development for the UNM College of Nursing.
As the leader of Nursing Education in the State of New Mexico, UNM’s College of Nursing offers an unmatched depth and breadth of education, research, service, and leadership within the field of Nursing.
The successful applicant will be responsible for creating and implementing a comprehensive development program in coordination with the leadership of the UNM College of Nursing, the UNM Foundation staff, and colleagues. The successful applicant will work closely with the Dean of the College, VP for HSC Development, SVP of Development (is this part accurate or will this person work directly with me for the most part and I will interface with dean, VP for HSC and SVP of Development? Just want to make sure I understand the interfacing before I talk to potential candidates), staff, volunteers, and friends to identify prospects, develop strategies leading to solicitation, and steward major donors.
The primary focus of the position is to identify, cultivate and solicit major and planned gifts benefiting the College of Nursing.

About the University

Founded in 1889 as New Mexico’s flagship institution, the University of New Mexico (www.unm.edu) has nearly 170,000 alumni from its culturally rich 12 Colleges and Schools, which offer over 215 degree and certificate programs. UNM is the only Hispanic-Serving Institution in the U.S. that is also classified a Carnegie Research University with Very High Activity. Recently, Hispanic Business Magazine ranked four University schools among the top 10 including the UNM School of Law, Anderson School of Management, the UNM School of Medicine and the UNM School of Engineering.
The University now occupies nearly 800 acres near old Route 66 in the heart of Albuquerque, a dynamic multi-cultural Southwestern city. Albuquerque and its surrounding area is the largest metropolitan region in New Mexico, known for high-tech industry, the world renowned international Balloon Fiesta, and its devotion to the UNM campus, programs, and athletics.

About the College of Nursing

In the early 1950s, New Mexico nurses voiced their concerns about an inadequate supply of registered nurses (RNs) to meet the health care needs of the state’s growing population. By the spring of 1955, the UNM College of Nursing was founded by Dr. Marion Fleck and Mary Jane Carter, with the enthusiastic support of UNM President Tom Popejoy.
Today, the UNM College of Nursing has over 1300 students in BSN, DNP, and PhD programs. We are the #1 BSN Program in New Mexico and rank in the top 17% in the nation. Our DNP Nurse-Midwifery program ranks #7 in the Nation. We give over $1.2M in scholarships each year and 83% of our students receive some form of financial aid. 71% of our students identify and coming from underrepresented groups.

The Rockefeller Foundation Communications team advances the Foundation's mission by strengthening understanding of its priorities, amplifying impact, and engaging key audiences through strategic communications, digital engagement, content development, and stakeholder outreach.

The Managing Director, Media Relations leads how The Rockefeller Foundation earns visibility and safeguards its reputation in a rapidly evolving media and information environment. The role sets the Foundation's media relations and press strategy, shapes its approach to executive visibility and reputational risk, and ensures a clear, credible, and consistent institutional voice across audiences and platforms. Reporting to the SVP, Communications, the Managing Director serves as a senior advisor to Foundation leadership and leads enterprise-wide media initiatives, working across the Foundation to strengthen its engagement with journalists and other key stakeholders in support of its mission and strategic priorities.

Work Schedule
: This role is on a hybrid work schedule and is required to be in the office on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. The role can be based in either the Washington, DC, or New York City office, with a preference for the New York City office.

Pay Range:
$230,000 - $280,000. This represents the present low and high end of the Foundation’s pay range for this position. Actual pay will vary based on various factors, including but not limited to experience.

Principal Duties And Responsibilities

Develop and lead the Foundation's media relations strategy—setting priorities, frameworks, and standards for media engagement, and translating institutional priorities into integrated media approaches—to strengthen visibility, reputation, and stakeholder engagement in support of mission impact across evolving news, digital, and emerging media channels.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the Foundation’s President and senior executives on media engagement, messaging, and public visibility—including media pitching, message development, and preparation for interviews and high-profile media events.
Shape and safeguard the Foundation's institutional narrative, ensuring talking points and messages stay consistent and in sync across Programs, Teams, and Regional Offices.
Position Foundation leaders and experts as authoritative voices with the media—providing coaching and strategic counsel and building and managing the public profiles of the President and senior leaders through high-impact op-eds, bylined pieces, speaking platforms, and executive profiles that advance institutional priorities.
Approve Foundation press releases, media statements, and briefing materials, and serve as a Foundation spokesperson when needed.
Oversee the day-to-day operations of the press office, ensuring rapid, accurate, and coordinated responses to inbound media inquiries.
Anticipate and manage reputational risk, detecting emerging issues early and leading crisis communications with clarity and speed, including partnering with the General Counsel on adversarial press, litigation-related communications, and sensitive disclosures.
Cultivate and manage relationships with journalists and media outlets, using coverage insights, analytics, and emerging trends to inform the most strategic pitching and outlet choices.
Provide strategic oversight of media relations operations, including budget management and agency/vendor relationships for wire services, media monitoring, and select media sponsorship opportunities.
Establish effective systems, governance structures, and operating practices that improve the efficiency, accountability, and quality of the Foundation's media function.
Partner with senior leaders across the Foundation and coordinate closely with program focal points and Regional Office colleagues to advance major media moments and high-profile events.
Manage outside consultants and agencies engaged for media pitching and strategic advice, and coordinate closely with internal teammates—including Digital and Internal Communications—to ensure an integrated, consistent approach across channels.
Provide strategic leadership and oversight to the Media Relations team and external consultants—building leadership capability, fostering collaboration, and coaching team members to create an inclusive, high-performing culture aligned with Foundation priorities, values, and performance expectations.

Generally expected to have 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in media relations, journalism, public affairs, or related fields, including significant leadership experience—ideally representing an organization with the media, serving as a spokesperson, or working for a top-tier news organization.
Bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, public affairs, or related discipline. Advanced degree in a related field preferred.
Experience working within philanthropy, public sector, nonprofit, international development, or similar mission-driven organizations.
Knowledge of and interest in foreign policy or international affairs.
Demonstrated success developing and leading enterprise-level media and reputation strategies for complex, mission-driven organizations.
Proven track record positioning organizations and their senior leadership, managing reputational risk, and leading crisis communications.
Experience advising senior executives and developing media approaches that influence internal and external stakeholders.
Extensive knowledge of media trends and established relationships with top-tier journalists and media outlets.
Proven ability to lead large-scale, cross-functional initiatives and drive organizational outcomes through influence and collaboration.
Strong people leadership experience, including developing talent and managing high-performing teams.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills, including public speaking and the ability to represent the Foundation with external partners.

Competencies

Action Oriented: Takes on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy, and enthusiasm.
Collaborates: Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives.
Manages Complexity: Makes sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
Nimble Learning: Learns through experimentation when tackling new problems, using both successes and failures as learning fodder.

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Our client, a national leader in emergency medical and healthcare products, is seeking a Chief Operating Officer to own the company’s end-to-end operating model and product engine: from product concept and engineering through sourcing, manufacturing, distribution, and customer support. Reporting directly to the CEO and serving on the Senior Leadership Team, the COO is the executive who turns enterprise strategy into measurable operational results — sustainable growth, margin expansion, regulatory compliance, and an exceptional customer experience for the first responders and healthcare professionals our client serves nationwide.
This is a build-and-scale mandate, not a caretaker role. The right leader will strengthen and expand our client’s manufacturing, distribution, and operational infrastructure; bring new technology and automation into the business; integrate acquisitions; and develop the next generation of operating leaders — all while holding the line on quality, safety, and compliance in a regulated medical environment.
What You Will Own

Enterprise Operations

Lead all core operating functions — Purchasing, Supply Chain, Customer Care, Warehousing, Distribution, Logistics, Engineering, Manufacturing, Assembly/Kitting, and Contract Manufacturing Management — with full accountability for performance, quality, cost, service levels, compliance, and scalability.
Define and execute the company’s operational, engineering, and manufacturing strategies in alignment with corporate objectives, growth plans, and shareholder expectations.
Design, optimize, and expand our client’s distribution, manufacturing, and operational footprint to support current and future business requirements.
Establish and monitor the KPI framework for customer satisfaction, quality, productivity, on-time delivery, inventory, safety, service levels, and profitability; report performance and risk regularly to the CEO and Board of Directors.
Serve as the executive escalation point for critical operational, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and customer experience issues.

Product, Engineering, and Manufacturing

Provide executive leadership over the full product lifecycle — product development, design engineering, lifecycle management, and manufacturing readiness.
Ensure engineering maintains rigorous, audit-ready product development practices: design controls, risk management, technical documentation, verification and validation, and design transfer, consistent with applicable medical device regulatory and quality standards.
Oversee manufacturing operations end to end, including production planning, assembly and kitting, process optimization, automation, capacity planning, and continuous improvement.
Bring new technologies into the business to drive innovation, strengthen competitive differentiation, and increase customer value.

Partners and Supply Base

Build and govern high-performing relationships with suppliers, contract manufacturers, logistics providers, and other strategic partners to ensure quality, reliability, scalability, and cost effectiveness.
Provide executive oversight of third-party manufacturers, including partner selection, performance management, quality oversight, contractual compliance, and ongoing operational governance.

Growth, M&A, and Leadership

Partner with the CEO and Senior Leadership Team to set enterprise priorities, evaluate business performance, and execute key strategic initiatives.
Lead operational due diligence, integration planning, organizational alignment, and value realization for mergers, acquisitions, and other strategic growth initiatives.
Drive operational excellence through performance measurement, standardization, technology enablement, and Lean business practices.
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing operations leadership team; own succession planning and leadership development across the operating organization.
Champion a culture of safety, quality, accountability, innovation, and customer focus, and advance our client’s Mission, Vision, Values, and Guiding Principles.
Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Finance, IT, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Human Resources, Legal, and Compliance to ensure enterprise-wide alignment.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12–24 months, the COO will be measured on outcomes such as:A unified, scalable operating model across purchasing, supply chain, distribution, and manufacturing with clear ownership and a single set of performance metrics.
Measurable improvement in margin, productivity, on-time delivery, inventory performance, and customer satisfaction.
Product development and manufacturing processes that are consistently audit-ready and compliant with applicable medical device requirements.
Successful operational integration of acquisitions with realized synergies.
A deep, credible leadership bench with succession plans in place for every key operating role.

Required Qualifications

Candidates must meet all of the following to be considered:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in medical device or healthcare products, including executive-level (VP or above) accountability for operations, manufacturing, supply chain, and customer-facing functions.
Proven success leading complex, multi-site operations in a regulated medical device, healthcare, or life sciences environment.
Direct experience leading product development organizations and bringing regulated products from concept through commercialization and lifecycle management.
Working command of medical device development and quality requirements: design controls, risk management, quality systems, and regulatory expectations.
Significant hands-on experience running manufacturing, assembly, and kitting operations, including production planning, operational scaling, and contract manufacturing relationships.
Demonstrated results driving operational excellence, continuous improvement, productivity gains, margin expansion, and organizational scalability using Lean, Six Sigma, or comparable methodologies.
Strong financial acumen with ownership of budgets, capital investments, operational metrics, and profitability targets.
Track record of leading large-scale organizational change and executing strategic initiatives, including M&A due diligence and integration.

Preferred Qualifications

MBA, Master’s degree in Engineering, or other relevant advanced degree.
Experience in a distribution-led business serving EMS, first responder, or acute-care customers.
Experience scaling operations in a private-equity-backed or high-growth environment.
Experience leading automation, technology enablement, or digital transformation initiatives across warehouse, manufacturing, or supply chain operations.

Leadership Profile

Executive presence and Board-level communication skills; able to represent the company credibly with customers, suppliers, partners, investors, and regulators.
Builder of high-performing teams and developer of leaders, with a bias for accountability and clear ownership.
Analytical, decisive, and strategic, with the operational discipline to balance innovation, quality, compliance, customer satisfaction, and financial performance simultaneously.
Entrepreneurial and hands-on: comfortable on the warehouse and production floor as well as in the boardroom.
Unquestioned integrity and ethical leadership.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements

This is an on-site executive role based in Dublin, Ohio, with regular presence in warehouse, manufacturing, and distribution facilities. The role requires approximately 30% travel (primarily domestic, occasional international); the ability to move throughout office and operational environments for extended periods and comply with all facility safety requirements; standard use of a computer and communication tools; occasional lifting of up to 20 pounds; and the ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive business information. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Benefits Snapshot

This role offers the chance to join a team that genuinely enjoys the work they do, contributing to a mission that helps protect and save lives. The company is steady, essential, and continuing to grow, with a strong commitment to diversity, inclusion, and sustainability. Its culture is built around its people and the things they care about, featuring perks like bring-your-dog-to-work days, travel discounts, gym membership discounts, and happy hours. The benefits package is comprehensive, including flexible PTO, a full range of health and wellness coverage, 401(k) matching, tuition assistance, adoption support, and pet insurance.
About Our Client

Our client’s mission is to be the best partner for those who save and improve patients’ lives. The company serves first responders and healthcare professionals nationwide, and excellence in delivering on that mission depends on a diverse, empowered team that brings its full, authentic self to work each day.
Our client is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We offer a competitive salary, commensurate with experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package, including a 401(k) Plan.
